subject: VLAN breakout & egress constraints for private endpoint — clarification and consolidated rules
messages:
From: Sam Hendrix <sam.hendrix@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: 2027-12-18T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Private endpoint in legacy VLAN — exact outbound IPs and firewall constraints

Hi Priya,

Quick context: we're standing up the Redwood private endpoint in our on-prem environment (Legacy VLAN: 10.20.0.0/16, NAT controlled by edge-router-01). Security asks for an allowlist of IPs (or FQDN-based guidance) we can use in our perimeter firewall to permit outbound traffic.

Constraints we have:
- No TLS inspection — we cannot decrypt customer traffic at the perimeter.
- DNS is split-horizon; our app uses an internal resolver (10.20.0.5) for service discovery.
- We prefer static egress IPs but can consider an outbound proxy if you recommend.

Could you provide:
1) A concrete list of IPv4 / IPv6 ranges we must allow (by region) and the ports/protocols required.
2) Guidance on whether SNI/FQDN allowlisting is sufficient for your stack or if IP-level blocking is mandatory for compliance.
3) Any ephemeral IP behavior we should expect during autoscaling or failover.

Thanks — we need this for our firewall exception request to the compliance team by EOD Wednesday.

—Sam
Sam Hendrix
Director, Infrastructure & Security
Greenfield Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Hendrix <sam.hendrix@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-18T11:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint in legacy VLAN — exact outbound IPs and firewall constraints

Sam — thanks for the clear context. Attaching an initial "egress-ip-matrix.csv" (stub) with candidate IP blocks and a short proposal for ports. High level answers up front:

- We support IP-based allowlisting (recommended for highest assurance).
- We can accommodate an outbound-proxy pattern (customer-managed proxy in your VLAN) that reduces the number of IPs you need to open, but that requires NAT hairpin / routing support so return traffic uses the same proxy egress.
- Ephemeral behavior: for Dedicated/private runtimes we offer a small set of stable egress ranges per-region by default; however failover (region fallback) can use additional ranges if you enable cross-region fallback. We indicate these in the matrix.

A few clarifying questions for your ops team before we finalize:
- Will you accept a small pinned range (<= /28) for the control plane + larger range for tokenized streaming traffic?
- Do you have a corporate outbound proxy we must route through (IP + FQDN)?
- Any internal IDS that will block connections based on TLS SNI only?

Looping in Laura and Karthik to confirm exact ports and the recommended firewall rule snippets.

I'll follow up with a consolidated doc tomorrow.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Hendrix <sam.hendrix@greenfieldhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-19T08:29:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint in legacy VLAN — exact outbound IPs and firewall constraints

Priya / Sam — technical notes and proposed firewall snippets below (we kept this intentionally prescriptive so your firewall team can copy-paste). See attached "fw-rules-proposal.txt" for an annotated example.

TL;DR: Allow TCP/443 to the stable egress CIDRs listed; allow UDP/53 only to your internal DNS resolver; block outbound TLS interception as it will break mutual TLS. If you cannot open the full stable CIDRs we recommend deploying a customer-managed egress-proxy (see pattern B).

1) Stable egress ranges (US region — final values in egress-ip-matrix.csv)
- Control plane: 203.0.113.16/28 (management & pingbacks) — TCP 443
- Tokenized streaming / inference egress: 198.51.100.0/24 — TCP 443 (note: uses multiple addresses for load distribution)

2) Firewall rule examples (perimeter edge-router):
- allow out tcp from 10.20.0.0/16 to 203.0.113.16/28 port 443 comment "Redwood control-plane"
- allow out tcp from 10.20.0.0/16 to 198.51.100.0/24 port 443 comment "Redwood inference traffic"
- allow out udp from 10.20.0.0/16 to 10.20.0.5 port 53 comment "Internal resolver only"
- deny out tcp from 10.20.0.0/16 to any port 443 when tls_inspect_enabled==true comment "Prevent TLS interception"

3) SNI vs IP allowlisting:
- SNI-only allowlisting is brittle for compliance; if your policy requires cryptographic-level assurance we must rely on IP allowlisting and mTLS. SNI can be used as a secondary control for monitoring/IDS.

4) Ephemeral/failover behavior:
- Autoscale across runtime workers will NAT to addresses within 198.51.100.0/24; these addresses are stable for the duration of a deployment but may rotate on kernel/instance replacement. We will publish a predictable rotation window (we propose 7 days notice for any broad change).
- Cross-region fallback (if enabled) will introduce an extra /24: 192.0.2.0/24. We only use fallback when regional health degrades.

5) Patterns we support (pick one):
A) IP allowlist only (recommended): open the control-plane /28 + inference /24, and configure your internal DNS to resolve our private endpoint names to the internal addresses we provide.
B) Customer-managed egress proxy (recommended if you want single egress IP): deploy an outbound proxy in your VLAN, route all app egress through it, and allow only that proxy's IPs to the Redwood egress ranges. This requires NAT hairpin on your edge-router to preserve source ip.

Action items for Sam:
- Confirm whether pattern A or B is acceptable.
- If B, share proxy IP(s) and NAT topology.
- If A, confirm you can open the /24 for inference.

We flagged the items in fw-rules-proposal.txt (attached). I'm also attaching a short PDF "safelist-sni-guidance.pdf" with trade-offs for SNI vs IP lists.

—Laura (on behalf of Infra & Runtime)
Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Engineer, Deployment Operations

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Hendrix <sam.hendrix@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-20T17:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint in legacy VLAN — exact outbound IPs and firewall constraints

Sam — consolidated guidance below (finalized after infra review). Please confirm pattern selection and sign off on the small exceptions list. We've also placed the matrix and rule text in a shared Drive.

Consolidated requirements (copy for firewall ticket):
- Allow outbound TCP/443 from 10.20.0.0/16 to these CIDRs: 203.0.113.16/28 (control plane), 198.51.100.0/24 (inference egress). If you enable cross-region fallback, also allow 192.0.2.0/24.
- Allow UDP/53 only to your internal resolver (10.20.0.5). Do not allow outbound DNS to public resolvers.
- Do not perform TLS termination/inspection at perimeter for these flows; mTLS is used end-to-end and will be broken by interception.
- If you cannot open /24, deploy a customer-managed outbound proxy (pattern B). If using a proxy, provide the proxy public IP(s) and we will restrict the egress ranges to those IPs (smaller footprint).

Operational notes:
- IP rotation: expected minor rotation within the /24 during maintenance — we will notify 7 days in advance for non-emergency rotations.
- Monitoring: enable SNI logging on the perimeter IDS for quick troubleshooting; do not rely on it for hard blocking.

Next steps & timeline:
- Please reply with "Pattern A" or "Pattern B" by 2027-12-22 so we can schedule the final on-site validation.
- If Pattern B, send proxy IPs and NAT diagram by same date.
- We'll prepare a simple runbook for your on-call and a short test plan for egress verification.

Attachments: egress-ip-matrix.csv (candidate ranges), fw-rules-proposal.txt, safelist-sni-guidance.pdf

If this matches what your compliance team needs, I'd be happy to join the firewall exception call.

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
